text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition staged one of the biggest rallies seen in the city of Lahore in recent years. Eight people were injured when a group of protestors clashed with police near the Punjab provincial assembly building.
- Just over six weeks after the last increase, the government has again raised prices of petroleum products.
- The joint petition filed by Ghinwa Bhutto and Badrunnisa, wife of Ashiq Jatoi, a companion of Murtaza Bhutto, was admitted by the Sindh High Court for regular hearing.
- The Commerce Ministry has finalised proposals for trade with India. They will be placed before the cabinet for approval.
- Pakistan's exports in the first quarter of the fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) rose 17 percent compared to the same period last year, Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar said.
- The cotton crop is likely to reach 9.53 million 200-kg bales in 1996/97, the U.S. Agriculture Department said.
- Pakistan's exports are likely to touch $700 million in September, 20 percent higher than in September 1995, Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar said.
- Main opposition leader Nawaz Sharif told Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto to quit honourably or be thrown out of power.
- The International Monetary Fund has asked Pakistan to cut defence spending by 30 percent, Finance Ministry sources said.
- President Farooq Leghari said Pakistan wants regional peace and stability, but India was producing nuclear-capable missiles threatening its security and escalating tensions.
